hypothesis: A first regular US National Hurricane Center discussion gives a more accurate 24-hour wind estimate than holding its initial wind constant, and an authenticated publisher URL with a UTC bulletin timestamp can be attached to an applicable research dossier.
scope: Operational Atlantic storm intensity, evaluated against a same-storm persistence reference. This archive contains no MEGALAB tournament forecasts. Incremental skill against MEGALAB and applicability to other subjects remain unknown.
cohort: Every AL01 through AL30 of the completed 2025 North Atlantic season. No storm selection by category or outcome. The first regular NHC discussion numbered 001 only, with its INIT and 24H columns in knots. One pair per distinct storm. A missing storm ID is distinguished from a real storm lacking usable guidance. No substitution of later advisories.
cutoff: Use the original bulletin's INIT UTC time and its explicit published local issuance converted to UTC. Give the evidence a 60-minute receipt allowance after the later of those times. Admit only a bulletin issued strictly before target and no future or corrected bulletin without an independently dated correction. The 24H target is the row's valid time, which can be 21 clock hours after INIT. No packet contains the later verifier.
verifier: NHC archived ATCF best-track B-deck for the same storm ID at exactly the valid UTC time. Use unique non-missing best-track wind in knots there. No nearest-time substitution. Post-event best track is used only to score the historical forecast.
statistics: Paired MAE in knots for the official 24H wind and first-bulletin persistence on exactly the same cases. Report storm counts, ties, wins and losses, and the one-sided paired sign test excluding ties. Also report source provenance coverage against the production configuration's zero directly retrieved primary bulletins. This measures traceability, not the accuracy of a fresh LLM replay.
gate: Retrospective support only when at least eight distinct systems have both arms and truth, the official guidance improves paired MAE, and the one-sided sign test is at most 0.05. Technical gate requires cutoff protection, issue identity, source allowlisting and graceful abstention on unsupported cases. Tournament production remains gated on an independent contest-relevant paired test. No inference, keys, or paid requests.
missingness: HTTP 404/410 means absent endpoint. Transient access errors, non-200 transport, antidateless, revised or ambiguous records are recorded separately. Failure to retrieve the season archive blocks a final skill claim; give exact eligible coverage among existing first bulletins and note short-lived storms missing verification.
